# Quaternius Medieval Village Pack - single bell

One unmodified original Bell.fbx selected for Where the Light Remains.
Creator: Quaternius. Original pack: https://quaternius.com/packs/medievalvillage.html
Creator release and linked original download:
https://www.patreon.com/quaternius/posts/medieval-village-45532344
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18T92VcNldHG0ugWo1u0hSJGDLua-n7o5

The creator's pack page and release explicitly grant CC0. CC0-1.0.txt is the
complete Creative Commons legal code, copied byte-for-byte from the project's
existing official legal-code record. It is not represented as the creator's
separate License.txt: that Drive request returned quota-exceeded HTML. The
explicit primary creator grant and full CC0 text are the license evidence.
SOURCE.json records both evidence URLs and this distinction.

The low-poly brass bell has a simple flared body and suspension loop, close to
the ordinary Paper Theatre bell. No tower, ornate support or fantasy decoration
is included. A hanging bracket/rope mount is not part of this source mesh.

Blender 5.2.2 LTS imported the FBX in a separate background factory-startup
process: one mesh, 405 vertices, 779 triangles, 0.633 x 0.633 x 0.733 m bounds,
one brass-coloured material and no external texture dependency. Its imported
material has Alpha=0. An opacity-only temporary preview was visually inspected,
retaining the original geometry and brass base colour. Set opacity to 1 or
assign the planned opaque paper material in a derived working copy. The source
has no UV layers; a simple/world-coordinate surface or small UV unwrap suffices.
The origin is (0,0,0), near the bottom rather than the suspension loop. Set an
appropriate hanging pivot and scale during the derived asset preparation.

Source FBX and license bytes remain unchanged. UE 4.27.2 import, collision,
lightmap and final paper-material validation have not been performed. No .blend
source, other legacy props or generated substitute mesh is retained here.
